notes: Hires are priced by the day now instead of as one lump. Each hire on the Plan step has a Days box, and the two money boxes are day rates: cost per day and charge per day, with a header strip naming the columns so three numbers in a row are not a guessing game. The quote multiplies them out - Sony FX6 x2, 2 days times 200 pounds day rate, 400 pounds - and a one-day hire stays a plain line, because the price already says it. The invoice bills the days as the quantity at the day rate, which is what an invoice should show. Hires you recorded before this have no days on them, so they count as one day and their old totals come through unchanged. The hint under each row does the maths as you type, including what the whole hire costs you over the days and the margin on it, and the cost offered as a one-tap job cost is now the whole hire rather than a single day.
